artists.biography:
Anathema are an English band from Liverpool. Beginning as pioneers of the death/doom sub-genre, their later albums have been associated with genres such as alternative rock, progressive rock, art rock, new prog, and post-rock.

Anathema formed in 1990 as a doom metal band, initially going by the name Pagan Angel. In November of that year, the band recorded their first demo, entitled An Iliad of Woes. This demo caught the attention of several bands and labels from the English metal scene.

At the beginning of 1991, the band gained a lot of attention with the release of their second demo entitled All Faith Is Lost, resulting in a four-album deal with Peaceville Records. Their first release under the label was The Crestfallen EP in November 1992. They took the material from that album on the road, touring with Cannibal Corpse.

Serenades, Anathema's debut LP, attracted a lot of mainstream attention, propelling their "Sweet Tears" music video onto the MTV playlist.

Anathema's first European tour was in 1994, and was closely followed by gigs at the Independent Rock Festival in Brazil.

In May 1995, vocalist Darren White parted with the band, eventually forming The Blood Divine. Rather than recruiting a new vocalist, the band decided that guitarist Vincent Cavanagh should assume White's role. This new formation debuted by touring with Cathedral in the United Kingdom.

The release of Eternity came in 1996, relying more on atmospheric sounds, and starting the transition to clean vocals; the album Judgement would later consolidate this style. A European tour followed the album's release.

perplexity.description:
Distant Satellites is the tenth studio album by British rock band Anathema, released in 2014 via Kscope. Musically, the album marks a further evolution in the band's sound, blending atmospheric rock with progressive and electronic elements. The record features a more spacious and less dense production compared to its predecessors, allowing the emotional depth of the vocals and songwriting to take center stage. The use of electronics is more integrated and subtle, with tracks like "Distant Satellites" and "Take Shelter" showcasing the band's ability to merge electronic textures with their signature melancholic melodies. The album also highlights the songwriting chemistry between Daniel Cavanagh, John Douglas, and Vincent Cavanagh, as well as the haunting vocals of Lee Douglas.

In the context of Anathema's discography, Distant Satellites represents a culmination of their shift away from their earlier metal roots toward a more expansive, emotionally resonant style. It is the first album to feature Daniel Cardoso as the primary drummer, with John Douglas moving to electronic percussion and keyboards. The album reached #33 on the UK album charts and was generally well-received, praised for its beauty, intensity, and emotional range. Critics noted its effective use of orchestration and electronics, though some lamented a sense of familiarity with the band's established formula. Overall, Distant Satellites stands as a significant entry in Anathema's catalog, reflecting both their artistic maturity and their continued exploration of new sonic territories.
